texts.facts: The factual matrix of the case is that the petition u/s. 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act was filed against the respondents submitting therein that the applicant was married with the respondent no. 1 on 20.02.2005 at Village Shikrao, Mewat, Gurgaon, Haryana according to Islamic rites and out of the said wedlock they have two daughters aged about 3 years and 1 years who are living with her; that her parents spent huge amount of money in marriage and gave handsome dowry including a Maruti 800 car bearing registration no. HR-36-F-7786 and cash of Rs.2.5 lakh, gold ornaments weighing about 20 tola (i.e 200 gms) silver ornaments and utensils weighing 3kg as per demand of the respondents; that respondent no. 3 took all her jewellery, istridhan and dowry articles in her possession and had not given the same to her despite demand; that since the day of marriage she was harassed by the respondents; that respondent no. 1 taunted her and called her ganwar (uneducated) and said that he has been married to a jaheel and unpad by her parents; that two days after the marriage the mother of respondent no.1 i.e. respondent no.3 scolded her by saying that she do not know how to cook; that when she said that she is not habitual in cooking on chulaha on this respondent no. 3 Digitally signed by GEETANJALI GEETANJALI Date: 2025.08.12 17:34:26 CA NO. 546/2018 MOHD. that she was constantly taunted, tortured and beaten by respondents for not bringing dowry as per their wishes; that in the meantime she became pregnant however there was no change in the attitude and behaviour of the respondents; that during the period of pregnancy she was told to do one or other thing or asked to consume one or other thing so that only a male child is born; that on 07.07.2008 she gave birth to a baby girl and she was taunted and maltreated for giving birth to a baby girl; that respondent nos. 2 and 3 said that their dreams of getting more dowry and car have been shattered; that after the birth of the baby girl, she was maltreated and tortured almost daily; that she was made to do all the household work despite her ill health and was not provided the special diet as required after delivery of a child; that she was sent to her parental house after about one month of giving birth to daughter and was not taken back after considerable time; that after great persuasion, she was taken back to matrimonial home by respondent no.1 after about one year and as soon as she reached matrimonial home, respondent no.3 took out the entire cash, jewellery and other articles gifted to the applicant and kept the same with her; that the baby girl was not given enough milk and was not even provided with proper medicine whenever she fell ill; that respondents forced her to call her father to give a Innova car for respondent no. 4 and when her father expressed his inability to give a Innova car, she was beaten by the respondent no.1; Respondent opposed the present petition by filing detailed reply taking preliminary objection to the effect that respondent no. 1 is still ready and willing to keep the applicants with him as per his capacity and earning and is further ready to maintain her but the applicants deliberately, intentionally and without any reasonable cause abandoned the company of the respondent no.1; that she had committed violence and cruelty upon the respondents and for the same reason no domestic violence as defined under the Act has been committed by the respondents upon the applicant; that the applicant herself is responsible for all the acts alleged to and attributed to the respondents and creating circumstances to seek divorce and has herself deserted the respondent no. 1; that on 19.01.2013 all the belongings/ dowry articles/ jewellery including jewellery of the respondent were already taken by the applicant/ aggrieved person at the time of leaving her matrimonial home and since Mohd Arif And Ors vs Zule Khan on 12 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169975881/ 3 then she is busy in filing the false and frivolous cases against the respondent and his family members; that the applicant/ aggrieved persons caused a great mental cruelty upon the respondent and always kept Digitally signed by GEETANJALI GEETANJALI Date: 2025.08.12 17:35:13 CA NO. 546/2018 MOHD. He was further directed to pay sum of Rs.2,200/- per month each to the minor daughters towards their monthly maintenance from 01.01.2013 till they attain majority i.e. December 2018. Trial Court has no territorial jurisdiction to entertain the petition under D.V. Act; that the Ld. Trial Court has further erred in not noting that the respondent no.2 has miserably failed to prove the domestic violence against the appellants and on the other hand appellant no.1 produced copy of judgments vide which he has been acquitted in various cases filed by the respondent no.1 and her father and that the Ld. Trial Court has arrived at a reasoned finding upon appreciation of evidence, the Appellate Court must be slow to Digitally signed by GEETANJALI GEETANJALI Date: 2025.08.12 CA NO. 546/2018 MOHD. Trial Court awarded Rs.5,000/- each towards compensation for mental injury and Rs. 4.000/- each towards litigation costs which is a modest sum, considering the suffering endured by respondent no.2 however the appellants have failed to comply with the said directions thereby demonstrating utter disregard for the judicial process and the rule of law; that the two minor daughters of appellant no.1 and respondent no.2 are living with their maternal grandfather as the appellant no. 1 has abandoned all his responsibilities towards their upbringing; that the father of respondent no.2 despite his meager income, is solely bearing the costs of their food, education, health, clothing and shelter; that in support of the above contention, school fee receipts and other related expenditure documents are being placed on record to illustrate the continued neglect and financial burden imposed on the respondent and her family due to the conduct of the appellants; that it is also important to note that respondent no. 2 has suffered persistent mental, emotional, physical, and financial hardship not just during the marriage but also post-separation due to the harassment and false counter-cases initiated by the appellants; that the Hon'ble Court at Nuh has already acquitted the respondent and her family members in FIR no. 726/2015 further affirming the malicious intent of the appellants; that the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has consistently held that women subjected to domestic cruelty are entitled to both compensation and legal protection, irrespective of whether they continue to reside in the matrimonial home or not; that despite being in possession of his salary slips and income records, the appellant no.1 deliberately withheld the same Digitally signed by GEETANJALI GEETANJALI Date: 2025.08.12 17:36:38 +0530 CA NO. 546/2018 MOHD. ZULE KHAN PAGE NO. 13 OF 29 during the trial proceedings and this deliberate suppression of material evidence pertaining to his financial capacity not only obstructed the court's ability to reach at just and fair assessment regarding maintenance but also reflects the malafide intention of the appellant to mislead the Court and such conduct amounts to an abuse of the judicial process and further fortifies the finding of the Ld. Trial Court against the appellants. Thus, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. The present appeal arises out of the Judgement dated 15.10.2018 passed in the Petition u/s 12 of Protection of women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 Act filed against the respondents seeking different protections as provided under the Act. Vide Order dated 08.11.2011 respondents were summoned but they failed to appear within the stipulated period and were proceeded ex-parte vide Order dated 22.05.2012. Vide Order dated 04.07.2014 the ex- parte order was [LEAKAGE_MASK] and respondents were given time to file written statement. Vide Order dated 11.02.2015, respondent no. 1 was directed to pay sum of Rs. 2,000/- each to the complainant and the two minor daughters total Rs. 6,000/- per month towards their maintenance. Coming to the first issue, petitioner has deposed that she was married with the respondent no.1 on 20.02.2005 at Village Shikrao, Digitally signed by GEETANJALI GEETANJALI Date: 2025.08.12 CA NO. 546/2018 MOHD. ARIF AND ORS . VS. He has further admitted that the applicant joined her matrimonial home where they lived together as husband and wife and the said marriage was duly co-habited and out of the said wedlock two female children were born namely Amna and Mowina aged about 8 and 7 years old respectively. Further the fact so stated in the written statement that "the behavior of the applicant/ aggrieved person was very cruel towards the respondents from the very beginning as the family members of applicant/ aggrieved person was very greedy and want to extract huge amount from the respondents" goes to prove that petitioner resided with the respondents in the shared household after the marriage. Secondly, respondent no. 1's statement u/s. 165 Cr.P.C that the complainant used to come to the matrimonial house after 20.10.2011 and finally left her matrimonial house on 19.01.2013 goes to prove that there was domestic relationship between petitioner and respondents at the time of filing of petition u/s. 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act. Hence the Ld. Trial Court has rightly held that: "the primary burden to prove issue (A) was upon the complainant. The Complainant has on oath stated before this Court that she was married to the respondent no.1 on 20.02.2005 and started residing in the matrimonial home at village Mevali, Tehsil Nuh, District Mewat, Haryana along with the respondents and out of the said wedlock, two children were born.
texts.arguments: It is well settled principle of GEETANJALI Date: CA NO. 546/2018 MOHD. ARIF AND ORS . VS. ZULE KHAN PAGE NO. 19 OF 29 law that if any part of testimony is not challenged in the cross examination that is deemed to be admitted. He has supported the version of the petitioner regarding taunting for not bringing sufficient dowry or not knowing how to cook and calling her ganwar, jahil or unpad and not providing proper food and care during her pregnancy. To him also no suggestion was given the Ld. Counsel for respondent thereby disputing the said allegations and the same remained unchallenged or unrebutted. 10.3. In respondent's evidence, respondent no.1 was examined as RW-1 and except for making counter allegations against the petitioner, he failed to give any circumstance which may belie the allegations of the petitioner. He has deposed that petitioner threatened to commit suicide either by cutting her nerve or by touching open wire or by consuming poison without any reason and now the question is that-"Will any sane person threatened to end her life without any reason" and answer is definite 'NO' and this is not the case of respondents that petitioner is not mentally sound. Secondly, it is the prime responsibility of appellant no.1 being the father and the husband to maintain his wife and two daughters but he even does not know that his daughters are school going. Further though he has stated that he is bearing the expenses of his daughters but has not led any positive evidence to show that he is financially supporting his wife and daughters and this amounts to economic GEETANJALI Date: CA NO. 546/2018 MOHD. ARIF AND ORS . VS. ZULE KHAN PAGE NO. 20 OF 29 abuse thereby depriving them all or any economic and financial resources to which Mohd Arif And Ors vs Zule Khan on 12 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169975881/ 12 they are entitled under the law and this is one of the kind of domestic violence as defined under Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. 10.4. Section 3 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act takes in any type of violence meted out by the respondents against the aggrieved person of much lessor degree and may constitute the domestic violence . 11. One of the grounds of appeal is that since respondents have been acquitted in the various FIRs, no domestic violence can be attributed upon the respondents and they have relied on the judgments Ex. RW1/A to Ex. RW1/D. The standard of proof under the Domestic Voilence Act is not beyond reasonable doubt but preponderance of Mohd Arif And Ors vs Zule Khan on 12 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169975881/ 13 probabilities. To prove a fact by balance of probabilities is to prove once version better, even slightly, than a version of other party. In the case of Rama Paswan Vs. State of Jharkhand in 2007 AIR SCW 2779, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that " it is cordial rule in the law of evidence that the best available evidence should be brought before the Court. The Court will have to depend on intercepted allegations made by the parties, or an inconclusive inference from the facts elicited in the evidence". 12.3. Regarding the guess work, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of Jasbir Kaur Sehgal (Smt.) Vs. District Judge, Dehradun & Anr. (1197) SCC 7 (supra), has also recognized the fact that "spouses in the proceedings for maintenance do not truthfully disclose their true income and therefore some guess work on the part of the Court is permissible. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has further observed that "considering the diverse claims made by the parties one inflating the income and the other suppressing an element of conjecture and guess work does enter for arriving at the income of the husband. It cannot be done by any mathematical precision". 15. It has been further contended by the Ld. Counsel for the appellants that the Ld. Trial Court did not take into account the Order passed by the then Ld. Principal Judge, Family Court, South East District, Saket Courts under Section 125 Cr.P.C. Vide said Order the Ld. Principal Judge, Family Court awarded maintenance to the petitioner @ Rs.6,000/- per month from the date of filing of petition till 30.09.2018 and Rs.7,000/- per month from 01.10.2018 till she is legally entitled to receive the same (this maintenance includes maintenance of daughters also) and herein Ld. Trial Court has awarded maintenance @ Rs.4,500/- per month to the petitioner and her daughters till December, 2012 and since appellant announced triple talaq to petitioner on 01.01.2013, the maintenance was awarded to daughters only @ Rs.2,200/- per month from 01.01.2013 till they attain majority which is much less than as awarded by the then Ld. Principal Family Judge, South East District, Saket Courts.
